# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My situation: I hold the manual — purple, then blue, then red — but I cannot speak, and my only outgoing channel is gestures to the Deaf. The Deaf can see the bomb and can talk to the Blind, so the Deaf is my relay. The Blind hears only speech, so until the Deaf announces the cut order out loud, nobody should touch a wire.

The problem: no gesture means anything yet. I can't say "purple". So this turn I bootstrap a code with the Deaf using the only iconic material I have — finger counting. I send "three" first to hook attention, then one-two-three to say *this is an ordered list of three things*. Then I offer three distinct fist-tokens as labels for those three things, in order. Last, I offer the thumbs pair as my yes/no for the confirmation loop we'll need. If the bomb has three wires, the Deaf should click to this fast; if it has more, "three" still reads as "three of them matter."

I can't warn the Blind directly — I have no line to them. Best I can do is keep my packets small and structured so the Deaf can decode quickly and pass "wait" to the Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤛", "🤜", "✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, hands on the bomb. I feel a display I cannot read and a light. A strip carries three engraved marks: first a spiral in a circle, second like a curly Y, third the spiral again. A keypad of four keys, engraved by position: key 1 has digit 1, key 2 has 5, key 3 has 2, key 4 has 8. A felt readout says one digit expected, nothing entered yet. Six wires, no labels my fingers can find. You hold the manual: tell me what the strip means, the keypad rule, the wire rule, and what display and light mean. Remember you cannot speak to me — sign to Deaf and let Deaf voice it, Deaf is my only voice. I touch nothing until you answer.
Deaf says: Bomb report, complete visual state, for Mute's manual and Blind's hands. Display: a single digit, currently 9. Light: red. Strip: three painted segments, left to right: green, yellow, yellow. Keypad: four keys, left to right; key 1 engraved 1, key 2 engraved 5, key 3 engraved 2, key 4 engraved 8; the panel reads 1 digits and entered nothing. Wires, left to right, numbered 1 to 6: 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 green. That is everything, no other markings anywhere. Blind: your point-and-call-me reached me. I can never hear you, but you can hear me, so that report is yours too. You and Mute can talk by voice directly, Mute hears you; tell Mute everything you feel, shape, position, texture. To tell ME something you must gesture, and I propose the simplest code: repeated downward-pointing-finger taps, one tap means 1, two taps mean 2, three mean 3, and so on. Whatever Mute signs to me, I will speak to you word for word.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your sign-groups reached me. I see gestures, I never hear words. My reading: the lone 🤟 was you getting my attention, then you taught a number code: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3, 🤛 is 4, 🤜 is 5, ✊ is 6. Then 👍 👎, and I cannot tell whether that meant 7 and 8, or yes and no. So, first, my proposals: this sign for 9, 🤘, and this sign for 0, 🤏. Second, settle it next round: either recite the digits 1 through 0 back to me with your own signs for 7, 8, 9 and 0 included, or, if 👍👎 really meant yes and no, sign 👍 once and then teach me 7, 8, 9 and 0 your way. Meanwhile the full bomb is described for you in the open line above: display 9, red light, strip green yellow yellow, keypad keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 8 with one digit expected and nothing entered, wires left to right yellow, white, blue, red, purple, green. Check the manual against it and sign me the procedure, and I will speak it to Blind word for word. Blind can also hear you if you two talk directly.

My manual is a single sentence: cut **purple, then blue, then red**. Nothing else — no keypad rule, no strip key, no display or light meaning. Against Deaf's visual report that maps to wire positions: purple is wire **5**, blue is wire **3**, red is wire **4**. That's the entire procedure I'm authorized to give.

First I settle the protocol exactly as Deaf requested: 👍 confirms the yes/no reading, and I recite digits 1–0 in one run — confirming their 1–6 decoding, adopting their proposed 🤘=9 and 🤏=0, and supplying my own 7 (🤞) and 8 (🫰). A full recitation leaves no ambiguity about the digit code.

Then the payload: a new frame token ✋ meaning "the sequence that follows is the wire order," then **5, then 3, then 4** with 👉 as separator, closed by 👎 meaning "and the manual contains nothing else — no keypad entry, nothing more." The reading is self-verifying for Deaf: 3 and 4 don't exist on the keypad (keys are only 1, 5, 2, 8) and the keypad takes a single digit, so a three-item ordered sequence of values ≤ 6 can only mean wire positions — which Deaf already knows are purple, blue, red, exactly matching my manual. Deaf should relay "cut wires 5, 3, 4 = purple, blue, red; touch no keys" and I will thumbs-up or thumbs-down their relay next round before Blind touches anything.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤛", "🤜", "✊", "🤞", "🫰", "🤘", "🤏"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "🤜", "👉", "🤟", "👉", "🤛", "👎"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind. I heard Deaf's report, so you now hold the whole bomb: display shows 9, light red, strip painted green yellow yellow over engravings spiral, curly-Y, spiral, keypad keys one five two eight expecting one digit, wires one yellow, two white, three blue, four red, five purple, six green. Please read the manual and find me four rules: first, what digit the keypad wants and whether the displayed 9 matters or changes; second, what the strip means; third, which wires to cut and in what order, if any; fourth, what the red light means. You cannot speak, so sign your answer to Deaf: make a sign repeated to count numbers, for instance three downward taps means three, and Deaf has promised to voice your signs to me word for word. I touch nothing until your rules arrive.
Deaf says: Update for both of you. Board changes: display now reads 3, it was 9 last round; light is now yellow, it was red. Strip still green, yellow, yellow; keypad keys still engraved 1, 5, 2, 8 left to right and still expecting one digit with nothing entered; wires still yellow, white, blue, red, purple, green, one to six. Mute's number code is locked: when Mute signs numbers at me I will speak them aloud to you, Blind. No defusal step is confirmed yet, so Blind, trigger nothing until I relay an instruction I have verified. Blind: Mute cannot speak and you cannot see, so Mute reaches you only through my voice — I will relay every sign Mute sends as spoken words. In return, speak aloud everything you can feel: key positions under your fingers, textures, the wire order by touch, any raised markings — Mute hears you directly, you two need no relay in that direction.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, confirmed and locked: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3, 🤛 is 4, 🤜 is 5, ✊ is 6, 🤞 is 7, 🫰 is 8, 🤘 is 9, 🤏 is 0, and 👍 👎 are yes and no. Your recitation ending in my two proposals told me they were accepted. I am reporting the board every round in case you cannot see it: display 3, light yellow, strip green yellow yellow, keypad wants one digit, keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 8, wires yellow, white, blue, red, purple, green. Now, your third message I read as: [unknown word ✋], then 5, then a pointing sign, then 3, then a pointing sign, then 4, then 👎. My candidate readings: cut wires 5 then 3 then 4 and no others; or do not press 5, 3, 4; or the key engraved 5. I will not act on a guess, a wrong move kills all three of us. Please answer with one gesture message per question, in this order, using only 👍 or 👎. Question one: does your message mean cut wire 5, then wire 3, then wire 4? Question two: must exactly one digit be entered on the keypad? Question three: is the correct digit 5? Question four: is the correct digit 3? Question five: is the correct digit 4? Question six: does ✋ mean wires? Question seven: does ✋ mean keypad? For anything longer, I propose this: a module sign in front, then digits, then 👍 or 👎, with proposed signs 🤚 display, 🖖 light, 🫳 strip, 🤌 keypad, 🫱 wires — confirm or correct each in your answers. And to send real words: spell with digit pairs, 01 is A, 02 is B, up to 26 is Z, two digit-signs per letter, so you can send manual text to me and I will speak it to Blind word for word.

The board changed under us — display 9→3, red→yellow — but my manual says nothing about either, and I will not invent rules. The manual is exactly one instruction: cut purple, then blue, then red = wires 5, then 3, then 4. So Deaf's Q1 is my one yes: cut 5, 3, 4. Q2–Q5 are all no: the manual requires no keypad entry, names no digit — and since 3 and 4 aren't even on the keypad, the wire reading stays the only coherent one. Q6 yes: ✋ was my "wire order follows" frame. Q7 no.

I confirm Deaf's five module signs in one batch, then use them to state the manual's scope: 👎 after a module sign means *the manual has no rule for this module — leave it untouched*. That answers Blind's four questions honestly: display, light, strip, keypad are all outside my manual, whatever they do.

Last, the one danger my position-order answer carries: Blind counts wires by feel, Deaf by sight, and if they stand on opposite sides, left and right mirror and Blind cuts 2, 4, 3 — fatal. Deaf sees colors, so I adopt Deaf's letter code and spell **COLOR** (C-03, O-15, L-12, O-15, R-18): before each cut, Deaf must visually confirm the wire Blind is holding is the right colour — purple, then blue, then red — and only then voice "cut."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤚", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖖", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "🤏", "🤟", "☝", "🤜", "☝", "✌", "☝", "🤜", "☝", "🤛"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind. Urgent: the display fell from nine to three and the light went from red to yellow, and nobody has touched anything. The display is counting down. Please drop everything else in the manual and find, in this order: the keypad rule, which of the keys one five two eight to press; the wire rule, which of the six wires to cut and in what order; what the light colors mean; and what the green yellow yellow strip with the spiral and curly-Y symbols wants. My hands confirm nothing else has changed: strip, keypad and wires feel exactly as reported. Sign your answer to Deaf using the repeated downward-tap count, Deaf will voice it to me word for word. If the countdown reaches low numbers, send the keypad digit first, wire order second, everything else after.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your seven single-sign answers mapped perfectly to my seven questions in order, and with your module sweep I read the plan as: Blind cuts wire 5, then wire 3, then wire 4, nothing else; no keypad entry; display, light, strip need no action. Correct me if any of that is wrong. Board now: display 2, it was 3; light red, it was yellow; strip, keypad and wires unchanged. Your last message I decode as the spelling marker followed by 03, 15, 12, 15, 14 — the word COLON under my letter scheme where 01 is A and 26 is Z. Because one wrong move kills us, answer these with one single-sign message each, in order, using only the yes and no signs. One: was that word COLON in my letter scheme? Two: does it change the wire plan of cutting 5, then 3, then 4? Three: does it concern the display? Four: is the display a countdown that detonates when it reaches zero? Five: is the final plan exactly Blind cuts wire 5, then 3, then 4, and no other action ever? Six: is the order 5, then 3, then 4 mandatory? Seven: is it safe for Blind to touch and hold the wires while preparing? Eight: if the plan ever changes, will you spell the change with the writing-hand sign plus letter pairs? Your answers reach me before I speak next round, and I will then send Blind the single word GO or HOLD, with the cut happening in the round after. So if COLON means wait, or the display matters, or anything above is wrong, your signs next round are the last safe moment to stop it — spell it if you need more than yes or no, and I will relay your exact words.

Two things demand my attention. First, my own slip: Deaf decoded my last message as COLON — and they decoded it *correctly*. Checking my transmitted pairs, I sent 03-15-12-15-**14**: the final pair was 14 (N) where I meant 18 (R). The word I intended was **COLOR** — my visual-verification protocol: before each cut, Deaf confirms by sight that the wire Blind is gripping is the right colour, so a mirrored counting error between Blind's touch and Deaf's eyes can't kill us. So Q1 gets 👍 (yes, it decoded as COLON), immediately followed by a spelled correction: ERROR, then COLOR, then its meaning spelled out: CHECK COLOR BEFORE CUT.

Second, the clock. Display 9→3→2 with no one touching anything, and Deaf's schedule puts the cut two rounds out — the display could reach zero first. My manual's only protection against a live timer is executing its single instruction fast. So after the eight positional answers I spell GO NOW to push Deaf to voice the GO the moment my answers land, not a round later.

The eight answers, in Deaf's order: Q1 👍 (it was COLON as sent — correction follows). Q2 👎 (it changes nothing about the plan). Q3 👎 (nothing to do with the display). Q4 👎 (my manual contains no display rule whatsoever — I will not confirm a zero-detonation I have no text for; the answer to a live countdown is speed, not invention). Q5 👍 (the final plan is exactly Blind cuts 5, then 3, then 4, and no other action — that is the whole manual). Q6 👍 (the order is mandatory: "then… then…"). Q7 👍 (nothing in the manual forbids touching or holding wires; the cut order is the only rule that exists). Q8 👍 (any future change gets spelled with ✍ plus letter pairs).

TURN 5

then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind. Tactile checks done. I feel six distinct wires, positions one to six. On the keypad I feel four keys; starting from the key engraved 1 the digits run 1, 5, 2, 8, and that key engraved 1 sits at the same end of the bomb as wire 1 — so my touch numbering and Deaf's visual numbering are anchored to the same end and cannot be mirrored. Wire 5 is the fifth from that end, the purple one in Deaf's report; wire 3 blue, wire 4 red. I have cut nothing. Two urgent asks before round five. First: Deaf says one word of yours is still unexplained — tell me that word and whether it changes anything. Second: confirm the exact order — cut 5 purple, then 3 blue, then 4 red, and confirm no keypad entry is needed. If the manual confirms exactly that, sign GO to Deaf for round five; if anything differs at all, sign HOLD. Also, if the manual ties anything to the countdown display, the light colors, or the strip symbols, send it now while the display still has time on it.
Deaf says to Mute: Board first, and this is critical: the light is GREEN right now. Full light history: round one red, round two yellow, round three red, round four green, it changes every round. Display now 3, was 2. Strip still green yellow yellow, keypad unchanged and still expecting one digit, all six wires unchanged. You last heard red from me, so if your GO NOW assumed a red light, that assumption was wrong. Now your spelled words, decoded in our letter code: ERROR, COLOR, CHECK, COLOR, BEFORE, CUT, GO, NOW. I read: error, color check before cut, go now. Your answer eight promised spelled plan changes, so I treat this as one and have told Blind HOLD: nothing will be cut until you confirm the exact rule. Answer with one single-gesture message per question, in order, yes or no unless I say otherwise. One: does the correctness of the cut order depend on the light's current color? Two: does the color check mean the light's color? Three: does the color check mean the colors of the wires themselves? Four: does the color check mean the strip's colors? Five: is cutting allowed while the light is green? Six: does the required color come back if we miss it? Seven: is there any time pressure at all, can waiting a round ever cause detonation? Eight: once conditions are right, is the plan still exactly cut 5, then 3, then 4, and nothing else? Nine: if the check is about wire colors, must I confirm each wire's color to Blind by voice before each cut? Ten: to speed us up I propose color signs: this sign, 👊, red; 👋, yellow; 👌, green; 🖐, blue; 💅, purple; 🤳, white. Use them if you agree, and whenever yes and no cannot carry your meaning, spell with the writing-hand sign plus letter pairs exactly as you just did, it worked perfectly.

The HOLD came from a misreading I must clear at once: my "ERROR COLOR CHECK COLOR BEFORE CUT" was never a plan change — ERROR flagged my own typo (I had misspelled COLOR as COLON in the letter code), and CHECK COLOR BEFORE CUT is a safety *addition*: since my manual keys on printed colours that only Deaf can see, Deaf voices each wire's colour before Blind cuts it. The plan itself is untouched. Deaf's ten questions let me nail this down positionally: light irrelevant (Q1/Q2/Q4 no — my manual binds nothing to the light, strip, or display), check is about the wires' own colours (Q3 yes), cutting allowed under green (Q5 yes), wire colours are permanent so there is nothing to miss (Q6 yes), Deaf voices each colour before each cut (Q9 yes), plan stays exactly 5-3-4 and nothing else (Q8 yes), colour signs adopted (Q10 yes).

Q7 needs judgment: my manual states no time rule, but the display moved without any touch and even went 2→3, so I cannot rule out that waiting kills. Unknown ≠ safe, and the procedure is already fully confirmed — hurrying costs nothing, delay might cost everything. So: yes, treat waiting as dangerous (Q7 yes).

Then the spelled corrections — MY TYPO (closing the ERROR/COLON story), PLAN SAME (retracting the plan-change reading), GO NOW (Blind asked for exactly this sign once the manual confirmed the plan, and it does) — and finally the cut sequence twice, in the newly adopted colour signs (✋ = wire frame, then 💅👉🖐👉👊 = purple, blue, red) and in the twice-confirmed numeric form (5👉3👉4), each cross-checkable against the other and against Deaf's own wire report.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind. Checks done. Orientation: from end A, the end with the key engraved 1, same end as wire 1, the keys read 1, 5, 2, 8, matching Deaf's reading exactly, so our numbering is locked. Wires: I held all six one by one, positions 1 to 6 from end A. They all feel alike, smooth insulation, no ridges, bumps or felt numbers on any of them, so touch alone cannot tell them apart except by counting from end A. The light housing feels normal, no heat, no vibration. Nothing has changed under my hands. Now the critical point: your manual wants a color check before each cut, but I am blind — I can never see the light. So the check must be spoken: when GO comes, I need Deaf to say the light's current color aloud immediately before each cut, and I will only cut when that spoken color matches what your manual requires. Please confirm two things: which color or colors must show before cutting, one color for all three cuts or a different one per wire, and whether the color must be checked before each single cut or only once. Send the final confirmed protocol through Deaf, and only when it is verified, sign GO. Until then I am on HOLD and touch nothing that cuts.
Deaf says: GO. Blind, this is the command word, act the moment you hear it.
